subject: Computing

unit.unitOverview:
Welcome to Unit 5 of Year 1 Computing at Ehel Academy. This is a warm, gentle unit about networks. A network is what we make when we join two or more computers or devices together so they can talk to each other and share. You already live with networks every day, even without the word for it: the tablet a mother uses to video-call family in Hargeisa, and the little box on the wall that gives the whole home its Wi-Fi, are both part of networks.

First, that a network is two or more computers or devices joined together. Second, that a network lets us communicate (send a message to a friend) and share (a photo, or one printer between many computers). Third, that many devices can join — a laptop, tablet, phone, smartwatch or printer — but some things cannot, such as a bicycle. Last, you meet the internet: the biggest network in the whole world, where we can chat with friends, share pictures and play games.
learningPath: Preview the goals, key words and the tools you will use
Read the concept explainers and study the code examples
Follow the methods and worked examples
Build the activities, debug your work and play the games
Apply, explain and finish the Unit Project and Challenge

provenance.transformation: Structured from the Cambridge Primary Computing 0672 — Stage 1 Teacher & Parent Guide, Activity Sheet and Mini-Project. Teacher-directed prose was rewritten into learner-facing explainers so the unit teaches with no adult present.

outcomes: Say what a network is — two or more computers or devices joined together.
Know that a network lets us communicate — send a message to a friend.
Know that a network lets us share — such as a photo, or one printer used by many computers.
Name some devices that can join a network (a laptop, a tablet, a phone, a smartwatch, a printer), and know that some things (like a bicycle) cannot join.
Say what the internet is — the biggest network in the whole world — and that we can chat, share pictures and play games on it.

concepts.title: What is a network? (we join together)
concepts.explanation:
A network is when we join two or more computers or devices together. One device all on its own cannot share with anyone. But when we join devices together, they can talk to each other and share.

Here is one tablet, all by itself. It is lonely — it cannot send a message to anyone. But watch. Now they are joined together.
concepts.example: Now they can talk and share. When we join computers together like this, we make a network.
concepts.checkYourself: Can you understand that a message can only pass where there is a join?

concepts.title: Which things can join a network?
concepts.explanation:
Lots of devices can join a network — a laptop, a tablet, a phone, a smartwatch and a printer. But not everything can join. A bicycle, a ball or a chair cannot join a network — they are not devices that connect.

Introduce the devices one at a time, with a picture or a mime, each in one friendly sentence
concepts.example: Answer this in your own words, out loud or on paper: Which things can join a network? Then check your answer against the explanation above.
concepts.checkYourself: Can you understand that some everyday things (a bicycle, a ball) cannot join? Can you name two or three devices that can join a network?

concepts.title: What a network lets us do (talk and share)
concepts.explanation:
A network lets us do two lovely things. It lets us communicate — send a message to a friend. And it lets us share — share a photo with someone, or share one printer between many computers so everyone can use it.

Go back to the human network from Session 1. When you passed the Hello note around the circle, you were communicating — sending a message. Networks let computers do the very same thing.
concepts.example: Answer this in your own words, out loud or on paper: What a network lets us do (talk and share)? Then check your answer against the explanation above.
concepts.checkYourself: Can you remember that a device must be joined before it can share? Can you name one thing a network lets us do — send a message, share a photo, or share a printer?

concepts.title: The internet, the biggest network of all
concepts.explanation:
The internet is the biggest network in the whole world. It joins computers and devices all around the world, not just in one room. On the internet we can chat with friends, share pictures, and play games with friends far away.

In our human network game, we joined a few children in one room. Now imagine a network so big that it joins every country — phones in Hargeisa, tablets in Mogadishu, computers in London, all joined together. That giant network is the internet.
concepts.example: Find one real example of the internet, the biggest network of all around you, or on a device you use. Say out loud what it is and why it fits.
concepts.checkYourself: Can you name one thing we can do on the internet?

concepts.title: Make a network (our playdough project)
concepts.explanation:
This session pulls the whole unit together. There is nothing new to learn — it is a happy chance to use every word from the unit: network, connect, communicate, device, share, internet.

Today you are the network builders! With your partner, make devices out of playdough — maybe a tablet, a phone and a printer — then join them together to make a network.
concepts.example: Do it yourself: make a network (our playdough project). Work through it slowly, then check what you did against the explanation above.
concepts.checkYourself: Can you name your devices, and say one thing you can do on the internet? Can you make or draw a small network with at least two devices, joined together?

esafety.title: Keep personal information private
esafety.text: Your full name, address, school, phone number, birthday and passwords are personal information. Never type them into a game, an app or a website, and never send them to someone you only know online.

esafety.title: Check before you trust
esafety.text: Anyone can put anything on the internet, so not everything you read is true. Check an important fact on a second, different website, and ask an adult you trust if you are not sure.

esafety.title: Tell someone if something worries you
esafety.text: If anything online upsets you, or someone asks you for personal information or to keep a secret, stop, leave the page and tell an adult you trust straight away. It is never your fault.

esafety.title: Respect other people's work
esafety.text: Pictures, music and writing belong to whoever made them. Use work that is free to use, and say where you got it. Your own work belongs to you — put your name on it.

selfAssessment: I can say what a network is — two or more computers or devices joined together.
I can know that a network lets us communicate — send a message to a friend.
I can know that a network lets us share — such as a photo, or one printer used by many computers.
I can name some devices that can join a network (a laptop, a tablet, a phone, a smartwatch, a printer), and know that some things (like a bicycle) cannot join.
I can say what the internet is — the biggest network in the whole world — and that we can chat, share pictures and play games on it.
